Entities, attributes and records

Unit 2 · Week 2 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the entities and relationships chapter, relationships-workbook.md, relationships-answers.md, equipment-model.svg and the four model CSVs (Borrower, Category, Equipment, Loan). Use fictional data and a disposable copy or paper. No SQL setup or student account is required. Explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Entities, attributes and records

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the equipment desk scenario from Week 1. Explain what each table, row and field represents. All activities are ungraded. Suggested timings can be adjusted. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

2. The facts that need a home

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and partner explanation

A label change could leave inconsistent labels for the same borrower in the flat register. A Loan row represents one borrowing event. Recall the separate homes for borrower, item and loan facts before introducing Category. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

3. Type, instance and attribute

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example with teacher explanation

An entity is one distinguishable thing or event. An entity type groups similar entities. An attribute is a property. In this relational model, a table represents the entity type, a record represents an instance, and a column or field represents an attribute. The value 2026-04-06 is not the field definition itself. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

4. A row and its fields

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Prediction and teacher modelling

Show L001 in model-loans.csv and compare it with L002. Ask learners to point to an entire record, a column heading and one field value. Keep DueDate as a date property of an event, rather than a permanent property of an equipment item. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

5. The new Category table

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired practice with exchanged roles

Category extends Week 1’s three-table sketch. Category assignments are a new design decision: Camera is Imaging, Tripod is Support, Recorder and Microphone are Audio. Model categories has three records, borrowers four, equipment five and loans six. A category may exist before any equipment refers to it. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

6. Annotated table definitions

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 1–2. E01 and E04 both have description Camera, so that description is not unique. EquipmentID distinguishes each physical item under the agreed rules. Ask for labelled examples rather than definitions copied without context. No SQL creation is needed. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

7. The column and the value

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

DueDate is the attribute or column name. 2026-04-06 is the value of that attribute for L001. A record includes the values for one instance across its defined fields. Ask students to use a different Loan row as their fresh example. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.

8. A fresh record

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

E06 represents another physical item even if its description matches E01 and E04. It requires a unique EquipmentID and a valid required CategoryID. No new loan is implied simply by registering an item. A sample’s unique-looking description does not establish a permanent uniqueness rule. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#entities-relationships.
